title.narrative: Global WASH Program (GWP) Phase II, Sierra Leone

description.narrative: Direct Project Participants At the micro-level, the programme will directly benefit 10,600 rural residents in 20 new communities in Bonthe District with access to improved WASH services. 6,000 people will benefit from rehabilitated EMAS wells and 3,900 from India Mark II well upgrades. 50 artisans will be trained in O&M using mobile technology, and 650 clients will access revolving WASH-related microfinance loans.At the meso-level, 50 district staff, including Bonthe District Council and line ministry actors, will receive capacity support to implement and coordinate the District WASH Plan. 20 CSOs and NGOs, 18 enumerators, and 2 media houses will be involved in planning, coordination, and awareness-raising.At the macro-level, 86 stakeholders, including ministry officials, private sector actors, media, and partners, will participate in national advocacy and coordination. Additionally, 20 WASH actors, 30 MDAs, 6 media houses, and 20 enterprises will be supported to strengthen policy, service delivery, and communication.Indirect Beneficiaries At the micro-level, over 225,000 people in 10 chiefdoms will benefit from improved WASH governance and infrastructure, including 750 VSLA members.At the meso-level, around 3,200 people, including informal WASH actors, benefit from stronger planning and alignment with the District WASH Plan.At the macro-level, national and international organizations (e.g., UNICEF, Concern) benefit from a stronger enabling environment with clearer O&M frameworks and enhanced coordination.

In Sierra Leone, Phase II of the Global WASH Programme (GWP) advances systemic change through three outcomes: Service Delivery Strengthening, Accountability and Monitoring, and Institutional Arrangements & Coordination—focusing on O&M improvements, district-level planning, and national sector leadership. Ultimate outcome: More coordinated and resilient WASH system in Sierra Leone has been established, improving the quality and consistency of water and sanitation services and contributing to better public health and livelihoods in targeted areas

This project is part of Phase II of the Global WASH Program (GWP) implemented in SLE, ZWE, PAK and India. Building on Phase I, Phase II of the program focuses on scaling and institutionalizing WASH systems strengthening across five key areas: Service Delivery Strengthening, Inclusive Planning, Accountability & Monitoring, Institutional Arrangements & Coordination, and Learning & Sector Adaptation. A key emphasis is the shift from systems strengthening to systems delivery, ensuring sustainable WASH services for target communities. Phase II embeds these approaches in government structures and policies, reducing dependency on external support. Advocacy and stakeholder collaboration remain vital for financial sustainability and institutional adaptation.
